definition: Effortful processing is mental activity that requires noticeable cognitive effort or task demand. In this source, it is indicated by greater pupil dilation, especially when a person is preparing for a more difficult task.

reasons: The packet does not define “effortful processing” as a kind of mental activity; it only says pupil dilation is a measure of task demands and effortful processing.

“Greater pupil dilation” for more difficult tasks is supported, but the broader definitional gloss about noticeable cognitive effort/task demand is an unsupported generalization rather than wording grounded in the source.

The definition’s first sentence (“Effortful processing is mental activity that requires noticeable cognitive effort or task demand”) is not directly supported by the packet; the packet only states that pupil dilation is “a well-established measure of task demands and effortful processing,” but it does not provide a general definitional description of what “effortful processing” means.

While the second sentence is supported (the packet reports larger pupil dilation during preparation for more difficult search tasks, e.g., difficult shape targets evoking larger dilations), the definition as a whole includes the unsupported general characterization from the first sentence.
